bastion_works.label: New bastion on the Travancore coast
bastion_works.anchor: A new red laterite bastion rising above a pale Travancore beach, bamboo scaffolding lashed along its face and an earth ramp where bare-chested labourers haul cut blocks; on the finished parapet stand bare-chested Nair musketeers in hitched white mundu, hair in topknots, flintlocks on their shoulders. Coconut palms line the shore beyond, and a flat bright sea runs empty to the horizon.
bastion_works.absent: No red coats, blue coats or hats on any soldier, no stone castle or foreign flag on the bastion, and no sail, ship or boat anywhere on the sea.

landing_beach.label: Beach below the new Travancore bastion
landing_beach.anchor: The pale beach below the new red laterite bastion, its bamboo scaffolding still lashed to the face, with a single longboat run up on the sand, oars shipped and a plain pennant at the stern. The landing party wades out of shallow, bright surf with their hats in their hands and bundles of paper held high.
landing_beach.absent: No drums, muskets or soldiers of any kind with the landing party, no blue or red coats, no warship close inshore, and no hat worn on anyone's head.

pepper_market.label: Travancore pepper market
pepper_market.anchor: A Travancore pepper market under palm-thatch awnings: open sacks of black pepper slumped on the ground, a brass hanging scale with coins in one pan, and a trader's low table piled with cloth facing a busy street.
pepper_market.absent: No chairs, glass or foreign goods, no foreign fort beyond the awnings, and the trader never takes Ibrahim's turban, scar or face.
pepper_market.time: daylight in the shade of the awnings

temple_mandapam.label: Travancore temple mandapam
temple_mandapam.anchor: The open pillared mandapam of a Travancore temple: stone pillars on a laterite plinth under a sloping tiled roof, a tall tiered brass lamp stand with open wicks, and a brass offering tray on the floor before the priest.
temple_mandapam.absent: No tall stone gateway tower, church, chairs, glass lamps or footwear inside the precinct; the coin carries no legible marks.
temple_mandapam.time: dusk, the brass lamps newly lit

ramayyan_room.label: Ramayyan's writing room
ramayyan_room.anchor: Ramayyan's writing room in the Travancore palace compound: limewashed laterite walls, a wooden lattice window, a doorway onto a verandah, woven floor mats and stacks of cord-tied palm-leaf bundles, with a low wooden stool for a visitor. Ramayyan sits cross-legged on the mat with his iron stylus and leaf.
ramayyan_room.absent: No desk, chair, bound books, bookshelves, paper ledgers or glass lantern; every leaf shows only faint incised marks too fine to read.
ramayyan_room.time: night, one clay or brass open-wick lamp

coastal_hall.label: Travancore coastal audience hall
coastal_hall.anchor: The Travancore coastal hall: timber pillars carved with vines and tigers on laterite bases, a sloping tiled roof on dark rafters, the long side open toward the sea, woven mats on the floor and tall brass lamp stands with open wicks. Whenever a view takes them in, the places are fixed: Varma on his low platform at the far end with his spear in reach, Nagoji the only man standing beside it at the king's right, Ramayyan seated low at its foot, Padmini and Revathi seated on the left, bareheaded ministers in white seated on mats in the mid-ground, and Lannoy at a pillar at the hall's edge, kept to screen right; closer views show only the panel's own people.
coastal_hall.absent: No throne, chairs, benches, tables or glass lamps, no soldier in a blue or red coat, and the only guards are bare-chested Nairs with sword and round shield. The visitors hold their tricornes in hand and nobody wears a hat indoors; every paper and leaf shows only faint marks with no legible writing.
coastal_hall.time: daytime, bright glare at the doorway and open side, brass lamps lit along the pillars

hall_verandah.label: Verandah of the coastal hall above the sea
hall_verandah.anchor: The long verandah outside the Travancore coastal hall: carved timber posts under deep tiled eaves, a plank floor and a low wooden rail, with coconut palms and then the open sea beyond. The speakers stand at or near the rail with the sea behind them.
hall_verandah.absent: No stone balustrade, glass windows, chairs or benches, no ship close inshore, and no envoys, scribes or guards left on the verandah.
hall_verandah.time: late afternoon, a low gold sun over the sea

nagoji_room.label: Nagoji's room at night
nagoji_room.anchor: Nagoji's small room in the Travancore palace compound: limewashed laterite walls, a woven mat with a low wooden writing board, a reed pen and a small brass ink pot, a clay open-wick oil lamp, a doorway in a plain timber frame and a wooden-shuttered window that opens inland toward dark hills.
nagoji_room.absent: No chair, desk, bed frame, candle, glass lantern or quill; the few sheets of paper are angled away and show only faint strokes.
nagoji_room.time: night, a single clay lamp throwing large shadows

character_notes.nagoji: Thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and jaw with no beard or facial scar, and a tiny flush gold ear stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. BLACK hair in a high Kerala topknot with only a first touch of grey at the temples, never the grey or turbaned figures on his sheet, and the silver chain of office on his chest everywhere except the morning doorway of Ramayyan's writing room, where he wears none yet.
character_notes.varma: Face, moustache and build from his sheet, with black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure. Throughout this formal audience he wears the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare-chested in cream and gold cloth with gold necklaces, his spear within reach; never a crown.
character_notes.ramayyan: Thin sharp features and receding hair, plain unbordered white cloth, no forehead marks or sacred thread, with his palm-leaf bundles and iron stylus; never the temple priest's face.
character_notes.padmini: In her fifties, thick hair still mostly black with a few threads of grey, coiled at the nape; a cream sari with a narrow gold border in the old Kerala drape with no stitched blouse, simple gold and a long walking stick.
character_notes.revathi: Deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, a necklace of flat gold coins rather than the round beads on her sheet, gold armlets and bangles. The sandalwood line at the hairline is her only forehead mark: no red dot, no sindoor and no tali, as she is still a widow.
character_notes.eustachius: Tall, his own pale wavy hair tied back with a black ribbon, no wig and no hat, in the plain white cotton tunic-coat, white ankle-length mundu and sandals of his sheet, never a blue coat. A straight sword hangs at his hip with its hilt wrapped in local cloth, and in the hall he keeps to his pillar at the screen-right edge.
character_notes.dutch_envoys: The senior envoy is in his fifties and heavy-lidded, in a grey powdered wig and a charcoal coat with only a thin lace trim at the cuff, his black tricorne held to his chest; the younger is in his twenties and thin, his own brown hair tied back with no wig, in a brown coat with his tricorne in hand. The scribes are bareheaded pale-skinned clerks in plain grey coats and the interpreter is a younger local man, empty-handed, in a coloured-border shoulder cloth; nobody in the party wears the blue company soldier's coat.
character_notes.ibrahim: Shorter than the fishermen but broader, white turban, short grey-flecked beard and a thin pale scar from the anatomical LEFT ear to the jaw, nothing on the forehead. A dark short coat over a pale vest with bulging pockets and a white mundu.
character_notes.yusuf: Tall and lean, white skullcap, neatly trimmed dark beard, a sea captain's short coat over a white tunic, no vest, no turban and no facial scar; never Ibrahim's face.
character_notes.temple_priest: The temple-priest face belongs only to the officiating Hindu priest at the lamp stand; the plump merchant bowing before him has his own unrelated face.
